core_obligations: Prove the equivalence between R-universality, preservation of irreducible rational representations after real extension, and Tits division-algebra preservation.
Force all nontrivial star actions to have a common imaginary quadratic inner field and coincide with real conjugation.

Use weights supported on different simple factors to detect quaternion-class cancellations and prove equality of all nontrivial invariant Tits classes. Use an outer nonfixed weight to force splitting of inner-factor Tits algebras over the common field; check the compressed converse for every global dominant weight without granting it as background.

proof_roadmap.step: Pass from arbitrary real representations to unique irreducible highest-weight forms, then use endomorphism division algebras.
A generic star-orbit weight detects the minimal inner field via the center; real division forces an imaginary quadratic field, and root-lattice shifts identify the two star actions.
A single factor representation and sums of invariant factor weights force conditions1–3 through quaternion cancellation.

Mixed weights detect the common-field splitting requirement. For sufficiency, apply the same Tits character/center calculus to fixed and nonfixed global weights, keeping the common-field and outer-factor splitting obligations visible.

difficulty_reason: After the external Tits descent theorem is allowed, this task still requires a global compatibility argument that is absent for an individual simple factor: all star actions must be aligned over one imaginary quadratic field, cancellation of real quaternion obstructions must force equality over Q, and mixed inner/outer weights must detect field splitting. The retained local reduction and the all-weight converse are part of the solution. This coordinated Galois/Brauer obstruction analysis exceeds a routine qualifying-exam calculation; no H3 is claimed, and the reader must assess the author compressed converse explicitly.

editorial_notes: The task counts the final semisimple direct-sum criterion only. The existence of some universal rational form(Proposition1.2, old item2007), separate classical-type classifications and the restriction-of-scalars proposition are not additional counted claims.

In927, the second factor is printed with lambda_i again. The preceding923–924 and following931–933 explicitly use lambda_i and lambda_j. Both real factors are H under the hypotheses, so this duplicated index does not change the calculation; preserve the original formula and disclose the index.

The source explicitly writes in912 that only the forward direction is displayed and that the argument is reversible. The allowed-input boundary does not supply the converse as a theorem. The solver still has to check all global dominant weights: star-fixed weights give products of the common quaternion class, and non-star-fixed weights have center L. For the latter case, the Tits classes of an already R-universal outer factor split over its inner field L, using the retained root-lattice invariance and weight-center reasoning461–492. This is the scope of the author compressed reversibility claim; it is flagged for independent completeness review rather than adding an alternate authored proof.

When comparing Tits algebras after tensor products, tilde denotes Brauer equivalence; D itself is the division representative. A product H tensor H is matrix algebra/Brauer trivial, not a division algebra. The source uses that distinction in921–933.
